places.name: Medina of Tunis
places.ai_summary: A UNESCO World Heritage site, the Medina of Tunis is a labyrinth of narrow streets, historic mosques, and vibrant souks.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning to avoid crowds.

places.place_tip: Explore the souks for unique handicrafts and local delicacies.

attribution.title: Medina old Town of Tunis
attribution.author: IssamBarhoumi
attribution.description: A global view of la Medina old Town of Tunis

places.name: Bardo National Museum
places.ai_summary: The Bardo National Museum is home to one of the world's largest collections of Roman mosaics and other historical artifacts.

opening_hours.notes: Last admission one hour before closing.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the mosaic of Virgil, one of the museum's highlights.

attribution.title: Bardo Museum - Carthage room
attribution.author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution.description:
Carthage Hall, Bardo Museum, Tunis, Tunisia.

The statue of an unidentified Roman empress in the middle, flanked by two headless statues of Dionysus. cf. Category:Ancient Roman statues in the Bardo National Museum.

Foreground: the altar of the Gens Augusta.

places.name: Carthage Ruins
places.ai_summary: The ancient ruins of Carthage offer a glimpse into the city's rich history as a major power in the Mediterranean.

opening_hours.notes: Guided tours are available.

places.place_tip: Wear comfortable shoes for exploring the vast site.

attribution.title: Acropolium
attribution.author: Niels Elgaard Larsen - (WT-en) Elgaard at English Wikivoyage

places.name: Sidi Bou Said Village
places.ai_summary: Sidi Bou Said is a charming village known for its whitewashed buildings with blue doors and windows, offering stunning views of the Mediterranean.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Visit the local cafes for a taste of traditional Tunisian coffee.

attribution.title: Sidi Chebaan
attribution.author: Mohamed Moslem Mosbah
attribution.description: the beautiful coffe "Sidi Chebaan" in sidi bousaid with one of the best views in the world :)

places.name: Zitouna Mosque
places.ai_summary: The Zitouna Mosque is the oldest mosque in Tunis, known for its impressive architecture and historical significance.

opening_hours.notes: Non-Muslim visitors are allowed only in the courtyard.

places.place_tip: Respect the dress code: modest clothing is required.
places.address: Rue de la Zitouna, Tunis, Tunisia

attribution.title: Mosquée zitouna tunis
attribution.author: Ben guedria houcine
attribution.description: This is a photo of the protected monument identified by the ID 11-90 in Tunisia.

places.name: Kasbah Square
places.ai_summary: Kasbah Square is a historic square in the heart of Tunis, surrounded by important government buildings and museums.

opening_hours.notes: A great place to start a walking tour of Tunis.

places.place_tip: Check out the nearby cafes for a quick snack or drink.
places.address: Place de la Kasbah, Tunis, Tunisia

places.name: Dar Ben Abdallah Museum
places.ai_summary: This museum, located in a beautiful palace, showcases Tunisian art and history, including traditional clothing and jewelry.

opening_hours.notes: Guided tours are available in multiple languages.

places.place_tip: Visit the gift shop for unique Tunisian souvenirs.
places.address: Rue de la Médina, Tunis, Tunisia

attribution.title: Dar Ben Abdallah
attribution.author: Sup'Comian boy
attribution.description: This is a photo of the protected monument identified by the ID 11-106 in Tunisia.

places.name: Belvedere Park
places.ai_summary: A large public park in Tunis, Belvedere Park is perfect for a leisurely stroll, a picnic, or enjoying views of the city.

opening_hours.notes: The park is larger and more beautiful in spring.

places.place_tip: Bring a camera for stunning panoramic views of Tunis.
places.address: Avenue de la Liberté, Tunis, Tunisia

places.name: Carthage Museum
places.ai_summary: The Carthage Museum offers a comprehensive overview of the history of Carthage and its ruins, with many artifacts on display.

opening_hours.notes: Located near the Carthage Ruins.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with the nearby ruins for a full day of exploration.

attribution.title: Facade Musee Carthage
attribution.author: nonanet
attribution.description: Façade du Musée national de Carthage (Tunisie)

places.name: Cathedral of St. Vincent de Paul
places.ai_summary: This cathedral is an architectural masterpiece, known for its stunning stained glass windows and impressive organ.
places.name_english: Cathedral of St. Vincent de Paul

opening_hours.notes: Check for mass times if you wish to attend a service.

places.place_tip: Take a moment to enjoy the peaceful atmosphere inside.
places.address: Rue de la Cathédrale, Tunis, Tunisia

attribution.title: Cathedral of St. Vincent de Paul
attribution.author: Bernard Gagnon
attribution.description: Cathedral of St. Vincent de Paul, Tunis, Tunisia

places.name: La Marsa Beach
places.ai_summary: A popular beach destination near Tunis, La Marsa Beach is known for its fine sand and clear waters, ideal for swimming and sunbathing.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Bring your own umbrella and snacks, as facilities are limited.

places.name: Roman Baths of Antoninus
places.ai_summary: These well-preserved Roman baths are a testament to the engineering prowess of the ancient Romans and offer a glimpse into the past.

opening_hours.notes: Guided tours are available in multiple languages.

places.place_tip: Combine with a visit to the nearby Carthage Museum.

places.name: Lake of Tunis
places.ai_summary: A large lake located to the north of Tunis, popular for its scenic views and as a spot for bird watching.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Bring binoculars for bird watching, especially during migration seasons.

places.name: Souk El Attarine
places.ai_summary: A traditional market in the Medina of Tunis, Souk El Attarine is famous for its spices, perfumes, and local handicrafts.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning for the freshest spices.

places.place_tip: Bargaining is expected, so don't hesitate to negotiate prices.

attribution.title: Souks Tunis
attribution.author: Free On Line Photos
attribution.description: Cuivres dans les souks de Tunis (Tunisie)

places.name: Dar Lasram Palace
places.ai_summary: A historic palace in Tunis, Dar Lasram is known for its beautiful architecture and as a center for Tunisian arts and crafts.

opening_hours.notes: Guided tours are available in multiple languages.

places.place_tip: Attend a workshop if available, to learn about traditional Tunisian crafts.
places.address: Rue de la Kasbah, Tunis, Tunisia

attribution.title: Patio principal du Dar Lasram
attribution.author: Annie Noelle
attribution.description: Patio principal du Dar Lasram, palais du XVIII<sup>e</sup> siècle dans la médina de Tunis

places.name: Bab El Bhar (Porte de France)
places.ai_summary: Bab El Bhar, also known as the Porte de France, is a historic gate in Tunis that offers great views of the city and the Mediterranean.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited at sunrise or sunset for stunning views.

places.place_tip: Great spot for photography, especially during the golden hour.

attribution.description:

Port de France, Tunis.

places.name: Carthage Amphitheatre
places.ai_summary: The Carthage Amphitheatre is a well-preserved Roman theatre that still hosts performances and events today.

opening_hours.notes: Check the schedule for events and performances.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with the nearby Carthage Museum and Roman Baths.

places.name: National Theatre of Tunis
places.ai_summary: The National Theatre of Tunis is the premier venue for theatrical performances in Tunisia, showcasing local and international productions.

opening_hours.notes: Check the schedule for current and upcoming performances.

places.place_tip: Book tickets in advance for popular shows.

attribution.author: Unknown authorUnknown author
attribution.description: Ahmed II Bey

places.name: Rue Charles de Gaulle Walk
places.ai_summary: A pleasant walk along Rue Charles de Gaulle offers a mix of local shops, cafes, and views of the Tunis skyline.

opening_hours.notes: Best time to visit is early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Stop by the local bakeries for a taste of Tunisian pastries.
places.address: Rue Charles de Gaulle, Tunis, Tunisia

attribution.title: Charles de Gaulle 1943 Tunisia
attribution.author: Marjory Collins
attribution.description: Carthage, Tunisia. General de Gaulle, accompanied by General Mast, saluting as the band plays Marseillaise outside the summer palace of the bey of Tunis.

places.name: La Marsa Corniche
places.ai_summary: The La Marsa Corniche is a scenic coastal road perfect for a leisurely drive, walk, or bike ride, with beautiful views of the Mediterranean.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the early morning or late afternoon.

places.place_tip: Bring a bicycle for a more enjoyable experience.
